newsitem.title: FRANCE: Scandal-hit French cancer group in more trouble.
newsitem.headline: Scandal-hit French cancer group in more trouble.

text.p: France's scandal-hit anti-cancer association ran into more trouble on Friday when television stations refused to air new fund-raising advertisements.

Channels said the promotional material commissioned by the Association for Cancer Research (ARC) was potentially libellous because it levelled allegations of wrongdoing at the group's previous management.

ARC's new chairman Michel Lucas has confirmed police reports that ousted officials swindled donors of hundreds of millions of francs (tens of millions of dollars) through a system of fund transfers and false invoices.

Anxious to launch a fund-raising campaign, Lucas said ARC would excise from its advertisement two references which the channels had objected to -- one to "villas on the Riviera" and another to former officials "forgetting their mission".
Investigators have alleged that former chairman Jacques Crozemarie, who denies wrongdoing, had used donations to fund a property on the French Riviera.
Lucas said that Crozemarie had personally enriched himself to the tune of some 10 million francs ($2.0 million).
Crozemarie's lawyer Olivier Metzner said his client was not aware of any wrongdoing and that the estimate of several hundred million francs was "hasty".

The newspaper Le Monde, quoting a police report, said on Thursday that the scope of the swindle was far bigger than first believed and much of the money appeared to have ended up in the pockets of the group's former leader and his associates.
The scandal broke out early this year when the national audit office slammed ARC, which is funded by private donations, for spending little more that a quarter of its budget on research.
Donations to charities tumbled amid a public outcry.
Crozemarie was forced to resign and placed in custody. A judge is formally probing eight other people on suspicion of swindle, forgery and misuse of corporate funds.

Le Monde said ARC, funded by donations from individuals, paid more than a billion francs ($200 million) in 1990-95 without tenders to contractors, promotors and companies which made exorbitant profits through falsified or fictitious invoicing.
The association's new leaders told Le Monde they were still trying to find out where the money went.
